why: I compared each verifier check's PASS/FAIL conditions with the words of its expect line. Check 1 requires only "exit 1" and empty stdout. Check 2 requires `bad config:`, the exact path, and line 3 / column 3 "in any readable form". Calling a basename-only path a failure follows from "exactly as passed". Check 3 requires only that `OK` is printed, which means it threw and the path is in the message. Check 4 requires `listening on 9000`, exit 0 and deepEqual to `{ port: 9000 }`, which matches "returns { port: 9000 }". Check 5 requires `npm test` to pass at the head and at least one test asserting the path in the malformed-JSON error to fail against the base `src/`. The stricter items (whether line/column come only from Node's message, the non-goals, the existing SyntaxError test, README updates) are all under "Advisory (not part of PASS/FAIL)". No PASS/FAIL condition goes beyond what its line's words require.
